analysis.title: Macau Gaming: Oct GGR -10% yoy inline with lowered expectation. Eying Nov-Dec GGR trend to assess earnings revision momentum
key_insights: Macau October 2026 GGR was MOP21.7bn, down 10% yoy, broadly in line with lowered market expectations (Bloomberg consensus -10% per Exhibit 1).
Daily GGR fell to about MOP600mn in the second to fourth weeks of October versus about MOP1bn on Oct 1-7, a typical post-Golden Week drop. Last year had a longer tail of gaming demand.
GS attributes the slowdown partly to softer VIP and high-end demand. High rollers are sensitive to news on China's capital controls and stricter enforcement of global taxation on offshore trusts.

China's tax authority gave residents a 90-day window until Oct 22 to declare and pay back taxes to avoid penalties. Sands China said fewer high rollers visited its Macau and Singapore properties in recent weeks. MGM China disagreed, saying its premium mass database (players losing US$100k+ per year) grew high-single digits % yoy.

The daily GGR run rate recovered to MOP670mn in the last week of October from about MOP600mn in the prior 2-3 weeks. GS says it is too early to call a meaningful recovery now that the declaration window has closed.
If Nov-Dec daily GGR is MOP600-720mn (the ytd range), 4Q26E industry GGR would be -12% to -1% yoy and FY26E GGR -1% to +2% yoy, broadly in line with consensus.
GS thinks a GGR/margin inflection is less likely in 4Q26. It still expects EBITDA yoy trends to look better optically because the high base for daily opex will lapse and operators keep cutting costs.

Macau stocks are back at their lowest levels ytd, hit by choppy GGR, worries over weaker high-end consumption in China, and concessionaires' agreement to contribute to the Government Guidance Fund for non-gaming diversification.
Valuation is at a trough of 7x FY26E EV/EBITDA versus 11-12x mid-cycle. GS believes much of the GGR/profit/return pessimism is priced in.
GS expects dividends from Sands China, Galaxy, Wynn Macau and MGM China to be sustainable in FY26-27E and rates all four Buy.
Market share, Sep 2026: MGM China rose to 19.5% (+3.5ppt mom), Wynn Macau fell to 11.8% (-2.1ppt) and Galaxy to 20.3% (-1.4ppt). Sands China held 26.2%.
Industry GGR in 3Q26 was flat qoq and down 3% yoy in US$ terms (US$7,458mn). SJM was weakest at -24% yoy and MLCO Macau-only was -13% yoy.
Sep 2026 total visitor arrivals rose 16% yoy, with overnight visitors up 6% and same-day visitors up 24%. Oct 2026 GGR was 82% of the FY19 level, with 10M26 GGR at MOP208.8bn.

sector_views.rationale: Valuation is at a trough (7x FY26E EV/EBITDA vs 11-12x mid-cycle), dividends look sustainable, and GS says much of the GGR/profit pessimism is priced in. A GGR/margin inflection in 4Q26 is unlikely, but EBITDA yoy trends should look better as the opex base laps.

earnings_insights: GS expects 4Q26E Macau industry GGR of -12% to -1% yoy if Nov-Dec daily GGR is MOP600-720mn (GS scenario, not reported).
GS expects FY26E industry GGR of -1% to +2% yoy in the same scenario, broadly in line with consensus (estimate).
GS expects EBITDA yoy trends to look better optically in coming periods as the high base for daily opex laps and operators cut costs (estimate).

Sands China commented on its results call that fewer high rollers visited its Macau and Singapore properties in recent weeks. MGM China said its premium mass player count grew high-single digits % yoy (company commentary, reported).

FY26E P/E (ex-exceptionals) per GS estimates: Galaxy 12.4x, Sands China 13.7x, Wynn Macau 8.2x, MGM China 8.1x, MLCO 6.8x. FY26E EV/EBITDA: Galaxy 7.0x, Sands China 8.1x, Wynn Macau 7.6x, MGM China 5.7x, MLCO 6.7x (estimates).

macro_indicators.interpretation: In line with lowered expectations. It was 82% of the FY19 level and shows weak post-Golden Week and high-end demand.
The actual matched the lowered consensus, so there was no surprise versus expectations.

trade_ideas.description: Long Buy-rated Macau operators Sands China, Galaxy, Wynn Macau and MGM China (also MLCO, LVS and WYNN per ratings) on trough valuation and sustainable dividends
trade_ideas.rationale: Stocks trade at 7x FY26E EV/EBITDA versus 11-12x mid-cycle, and GS says the pessimism is largely priced in.
trade_ideas.risk: Weak Nov-Dec GGR and high-end demand, plus concerns over returns on the Government Guidance Fund contributions.

risk_factors: Weak high-end and VIP demand tied to China capital controls and offshore-trust tax enforcement.
Nov-Dec GGR may stay at MOP600-720mn a day, so there is no 4Q26 GGR/margin inflection.
Concessionaires' contributions to the Government Guidance Fund raise concerns about future investment returns.
Visible market share shifts and weakness at SJM (-24% yoy in 3Q26) and MLCO (-13% yoy).
charts_described: Exhibit 5 sensitivity: Nov-Dec daily GGR of MOP570mn to MOP779mn (76% to 104% of FY19) gives 4Q26E industry GGR of -15% to +5% yoy and FY26E GGR of -2% to +4% yoy.
Exhibit 12 weekly GGR: daily GGR was MOP1,025mn in the week ending 10/4, then 729, 613, 592 and 670mn in the following weeks.
Exhibit 1: Oct 2026 actual GGR was -10% yoy versus Bloomberg consensus of -10%.
geopolitical: China's tax authority gave its residents a 90-day window until Oct 22 to declare and pay back taxes on offshore holdings to avoid penalties.
The report cites news on China's capital controls and stricter global enforcement of taxation on offshore trusts as weighing on high-roller demand in Macau.
Macau concessionaires agreed to contribute to the Government Guidance Fund to support non-gaming diversification (GS report of Oct 26).

tension_points.bull_case: Stocks trade at trough valuation (7x FY26E EV/EBITDA vs 11-12x mid-cycle), dividends are sustainable, and the daily run rate rebounded to MOP670mn in the last week of October after the tax declaration window closed. MGM China's premium mass count grew high-single digits % yoy.
